body:
PROBLEM

`adlc-prosecute` computes the changed-file set for trust-root tiering AND the `git-change:` revision identity with a one-commit-arg diff against the RESOLVED BASE TIP (`git diff --name-only <base>` in `changedFiles`/`renamedSources`, `git diff --raw --no-renames <base>` in `resolveChangeSetRevision`). When the change branch is BEHIND the base (the base branch advanced after the branch point), that diff also reports every base-side file changed since the branch point (as reversed differences). Two production failures follow:

1. FALSE TRUST-ROOT TIERING: PR #493, whose real diff only ADDS `.adlc/tickets/**` shards and `.adlc/manifest.d/**` entries (surfaces #326 deliberately excluded from tiering), was classified trust-root with reasons naming `packages/**`, `plugins/**`, `.github/workflows/**` — base-side churn matching ticket rails (T37/T38/T53) and ENFORCEMENT_PREFIXES, none of it touched by the PR. The cross-model gate (.github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml) then demands a distinct-provider attestation for a change class the sanctioned review path cannot cleanly approve, making such PRs structurally un-mergeable.

2. UNSTABLE IDENTITY: `resolveChangeSetRevision` embeds the base-tip sha as the identity's base component and hashes base-side churn entries into the digest, so EVERY advance of the base branch moves the identity and invalidates recorded cross-model attestations even when the reviewed change is byte-for-byte identical. This is the same defect class #362/#367 fixed for the whole-worktree revision, reintroduced one level down; it is why carry-forward ceremonies and re-attestation-after-rebase are routinely needed.

FIX

Resolve the diff anchor to the MERGE-BASE (`git merge-base <base> HEAD`) before both computations:

- packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs: `changedFiles` and `renamedSources` (both the worktree and `--cached` scans) diff against the merge-base sha instead of the raw base. The diff stays ONE-COMMIT-ARG against the working tree; the untracked-files union (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`) is unchanged. Update the in-file help/comment text that documents the two-dot-vs-base-tip basis.
- packages/core/lib/revision.mjs `resolveChangeSetRevision`: resolve `baseSha = git merge-base <base> HEAD`, run `git diff --raw --no-renames --abbrev=40 -z <mergeBaseSha>`, and embed the MERGE-BASE sha as the `git-change:<sha>:<digest>` base component. Update the BASIS comment.

INVARIANTS TO PRESERVE

- FIX A (packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-cross-model-cli.test.mjs): an UNCOMMITTED edit to a trust-root file still tiers — never diff `<base>..HEAD`; always compare to the working tree.
- FAIL CLOSED: if the merge-base is unresolvable (unresolvable base ref, disjoint/orphan histories, unborn HEAD), tier-check refuses the run (existing opError exit-1 path) and `resolveChangeSetRevision` returns null — never fall back to the base tip and never proceed ungated.
- LINEAR-HISTORY EQUIVALENCE: when `git merge-base <base> HEAD` equals the resolved base sha (branch is current or rebased), classification and the identity string are byte-identical to today's behavior.
- The rename-source collection keeps BOTH the worktree and `--cached` scans (a merely-staged rename still reports its source).
- The gitlink/unknown-mode fail-closed path and ignoredPaths handling in resolveChangeSetRevision are unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with its concrete verification)

- AC1 base-side churn does not tier: in a fixture repo where the base branch advances AFTER the branch point touching a gated surface (e.g. a path matching an ENFORCEMENT_PREFIXES entry or a ticket rail) while the change branch touches only an un-gated path, tier-check classifies NOT trust-root. Verify: node --test packages/prosecute/test/tier-merge-base.test.mjs
- AC2 FIX A intact: an uncommitted working-tree edit to a trust-root file still tiers. Verify: node --test packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-cross-model-cli.test.mjs (existing test, unmodified)
- AC3 identity stability: resolve the change-set identity, advance the base branch with a commit not touching the branch's changed files, resolve again — the `git-change:` string is IDENTICAL (a recorded attestation for it still verifies). Verify: node --test packages/core/test/revision-merge-base.test.mjs
- AC4 identity base component: when the merge-base and the base tip differ, the sha embedded in the identity equals `git merge-base <base> HEAD`. Verify: node --test packages/core/test/revision-merge-base.test.mjs
- AC5 fail closed: with disjoint histories (no merge-base), tier-check exits 1 via the fail-closed opError path and resolveChangeSetRevision returns null. Verify: covered by both new test files above
- AC6 no regressions: node --test packages/prosecute/test/ and node --test packages/core/test/ are fully green
- AC7 load-bearing tests: adlc hollow-test --target packages/core/lib/revision.mjs --test-cmd "node --test packages/core/test/revision-merge-base.test.mjs" kills a merge-base→base-tip revert mutant (and the equivalent run for the bin's changed-file computation)

CONTEXT FOR A FRESH AGENT

- The tier classifier itself (packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs) is CORRECT and out of scope — the defect is the changed-file SET fed to it and the identity BASIS, both in the two files named above.
- CI (cross-model-gate.yml) invokes the BASE branch's binary with cwd set to a detached PR-head worktree and `--base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`; `git merge-base <base> HEAD` must therefore work from a detached HEAD (it does — no special-casing needed) and the workflow file needs no changes.
- Security note for the reviewer: a PR file whose tree content equals the merge-base content contributes nothing at merge time (git three-way merge resolves to the base side), so excluding base-side churn is FAITHFUL to what merging applies; an attacker reverting a base-side fix must commit a change vs the merge-base, which the diff reports and which tiers. This matches the diff GitHub reviewers and the cross-model reviewer actually see (three-dot semantics), closing today's gap where the attested identity covers content nobody reviewed.
- This change itself touches packages/prosecute/** and packages/core/**, so its own PR legitimately tiers trust-root: budget for a distinct-provider (agy) adversarial review + `adlc prosecute record-cross-model` bound to the final rebased revision.
title: Bind trust-root tiering and the change-set identity to the merge-base, not the base tip
